previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG and stents, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, diabetes, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for chest pain that occurred after a dialysis session and walking. The pain was typical of his stable angina, associated with back pain and nausea, and resolved with sublingual nitroglycerin. Evaluation showed no EKG changes and stable cardiac enzymes, ruling out acute myocardial infarction. He was managed with observation, continuation of anti-anginal therapy, and an increase in amlodipine from 2.5 mg to 5 mg daily. His insulin glargine dose was reduced to 6 units daily due to dialysis-related sensitivity. He remained pain-free, was discharged home the next day with instructions to monitor weight and continue medications, and advised to follow up with cardiology.

called on him one night because of chest pain.  His blood

signs/symptoms for pneumonia, the decision was made to not treat 
the lower lobe infiltrate.
